verses.1: Brothers, may the peace of my heart and devotion to the God be with you for your salvation.
verses.2: I testify to them that they have a desire for God; but not in a way that is recognized by them.
verses.3: For they did not acknowledge the justice of God, and instead sought to be righteous in their own ways. They therefore failed to accept the justice of God.
verses.4: For in the end, Christ brings justice to all who believe.
verses.5: Moses wrote that the justice created by law will be lived by those who uphold it.
verses.6: And the justice of faith says thus: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’” This is what Christ means by saying this.
verses.7: Who will be brought to the abyss? This is what Christ does: he brings people back from the dead.
verses.8: But what does that mean? The word of faith is with you, in your mouth and in your heart. That’s what the word of faith is all about.
verses.9: For if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God has raised him from the dead, then you will be saved.
verses.10: For the heart believes in justice, but the mouth confesses to salvation.
verses.11: For the scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will not be condemned.”
verses.12: For there is no division between a Jew and a Greek. After all, he himself is the Lord of all things. He brings wealth to everyone who calls upon him.
verses.13: For anyone who is called by the name of the Lord, he will be saved.
verses.14: How, then, can they be called to believe in someone they don’t believe in? How can they believe in something they haven’t heard about? How can they listen without being told about it first?
verses.15: How, then, will they be proclaimed if they do not go? As it is written: “How happy are those who spread good deeds!”
verses.16: But not everyone accepted the good news. For Esaias said, “Lord, who has believed our words?”
verses.17: Therefore, faith comes through hearing; hearing, in turn, comes through the name of Christ.
verses.18: But I say, did they not listen? Let’s see: The darkness of them spread across all the land, and their words reached even the ends of the world.
verses.19: But I say, isn’t Israel known? First, Moses says: “I will demand from you that you abandon your own people and instead work for the sake of all nations.”
verses.20: Esaias, however, dares to say this: “I found that those who are not sought after by me, become visible to me as those who are not worthy of being ignored.”
verses.21: But to Israel he said: “I have spent the whole day trying to control my hands while speaking to the people, so that I wouldn’t speak against them.”
